text:
Anya: Quick update — I ran the priority-tiering experiment where prefill requests go to a warm-KV lane for 100ms holdback, decode stays on fast-path. Wanted to share numbers and a weird regression.

Ben: Nice, what metrics looked at?

Anya: p50 gen latency down ~12%, p95 down ~18% for mixed short/med sequences. End-to-end throughput +6% on the canary cluster.

Kai: That sounds promising. What changed in batching logic exactly?

Anya: Two small heuristics: 1) split incoming requests by phase estimate (prefill vs decode) and maintain separate batch windows. 2) add a tiny token-budget cap per batch (default 64 tokens) so prefill batches don't grow huge and steal kernel shapes from decode. Also we tag batches with kernel-hints to prefer fp16 fused kernels for decode.

Maria: Any effect on KV cache hit rate?

Anya: Yes — warm-KV lane keeps a short delay to let KV priming complete for flows that look like multi-turn chats. KV hit rate for subsequent decode requests improved ~22% for affected users.

Sam: Regression you mentioned?

Anya: Observed CPU saturation on host-level for small-seq workloads (lots of tiny prefill-only requests). Looks like the separate prefill queue increased scheduling churn and more small batches triggered kernel launches, so CPU and kernel launch overhead climbed.

Ben: Can you paste the profiler snippet?

Anya: Sure — minimal repro run:
```
./perf-run --workload=smlseq-mix --batcher=phase-split --token-cap=64 
# perf shows kernel-launch overhead 38% -> 55% of time on small batches
```

Kai: I wonder if we should bound prefill batching frequency (coalesce for up to X ms) instead of pure holdback. A micro-coalesce plus token-cap might reduce kernel churn.

Maria: We could also reuse a hot kernel process for repeated tiny batches by pinning kernel affinity for the warm lane. That would lower launch overhead at the cost of slightly higher memory residency.

Sam: Any datapoints on latency tail after the CPU issue?

Anya: Tail worsened for pure small-seq customers — p99 increased 30% in canary. Mixed workloads unchanged. So it's a localized regression.

Ben: Action items?

Anya: Proposed plan: 1) revert explicit lane separation for tiny-seq customers via a routing rule (keep old single-queue for clients with mean tokens < 16). 2) implement micro-coalesce window (configurable 2–8ms) for prefill lane. 3) add a kernel hot-pool flag to reduce launch cost. 4) add telemetry tags: batch_shape, lane, token_budget, kv_hit.

Kai: Agree. Also add an experiment that varies token_cap (32/64/128) and the coalesce window to find knee. We should drive based on cost-per-token and p95 latency.

Maria: I'll sketch the PR with the hot-pool flag and the telemetry changes. Linking baseline run and profiler: https://git.internal/infra/perf/issue/2871 (internal).

deploy-bot: Deployer scheduled for canary on cluster canary-7 at 2026-03-18T16:12:00Z for the micro-coalesce test.

Sam: One more thought — add a counter for "kv-warm-satisfied" so we can A/B confirm the holdback actually yields useful KV hits before wider rollout.

Anya: Good call. I'll add that and post a short follow-up with the updated numbers after the canary. Thanks all :rocket:
